section_summary: This section records American and British oil companies’ objections to Japan’s 1934 Petroleum Industry Control Law, especially its compulsory oil reserves, annual licenses, price controls, and uncertain treatment of foreign refiners. It includes company appeals, a U.S. Embassy assessment, and a large compilation of the law, implementing rules, and related ordinances in English and Japanese.

people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: J. C. Goold
people.role: General Manager, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company in Japan

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Coe’s gasoline quota letter
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Department of State
subfiles.to: Kersey F. Coe, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Coe’s report on Standard-Vacuum’s gasoline sales quota in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests continued reports on developments under Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese oil storage and merchant shipping
subfiles.about: Links Japanese oil storage discussions to the strategic value of Japan’s merchant fleet.
subfiles.summary: Directs attention to Kobe’s confidential report for discussions in Washington and London.

subfiles.title: Coe forwards company appeals to the Japanese minister
subfiles.from: Kersey F. Coe, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Transmits letters from Standard-Vacuum and Rising Sun Petroleum concerning the Japanese control law.
subfiles.summary: Coe forwards the companies’ appeals and notes that copies went to their ambassadors.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum questions on the Petroleum Industry Control Law
subfiles.from: J. C. Goold, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.to: Chūji Machida, Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Seeks an interview and written assurances before committing capital to Japan’s required oil reserves.
subfiles.summary: Goold describes the law’s storage, licensing, refining, pricing, and inspection powers. Ten questions ask about equal treatment, future business guarantees, refinery ownership, tariffs, compensation, subsidies, reserve quantities, storage risks, and pricing.

subfiles.title: Hardships experienced by foreign companies under the new law
subfiles.about: Lists definite and probable burdens imposed on foreign oil companies.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites compulsory investment without secure business, uncertain refinery permits, controlled prices, possible loss of market share, Japanese tanker preferences, and military use of reserves.

subfiles.title: Rising Sun Petroleum appeal to the Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.to: Chūji Machida, Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Requests clarification of Japan’s policy toward foreign oil storage, imports, and refining.
subfiles.summary: The company argues that costly reserves cannot be justified under annual import licenses. It asks whether Japan favors domestic, joint, or foreign refining and seeks a secure basis for further investment.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Coe’s forwarded correspondence
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Department of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the two company letters to Japan’s commerce minister.
subfiles.summary: States that the Department is considering the correspondence.

subfiles.title: American Oil Interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Assesses the effect of Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law on American and British oil companies.
subfiles.summary: Grew details the required six months of oil reserves, estimated investment costs, licensing and price powers, and the companies’ unanswered questions. He reports their resistance to bearing storage costs and risks, while judging that Japan is unlikely to abandon a requirement tied to national defense.

subfiles.title: Hardships experienced by foreign companies under the new law, embassy copy
subfiles.about: Provides an enclosure copy of foreign companies’ objections to Japan’s oil law.
subfiles.summary: Repeats concerns over compelled investment, insecure licenses, pricing, market share, tanker use, and military stock requirements.

subfiles.title: Despatch 938 identification sheet
subfiles.about: Identifies the accompanying material as part of despatch 938.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten identification of the Tokyo despatch.

subfiles.title: Petroleum Industry Control Law: Japan, Korea, Formosa
subfiles.about: Introduces a compilation of Japanese petroleum control documents.
subfiles.summary: Title page naming Japan, Korea, and Formosa.

subfiles.title: Official documents relating to the control law
subfiles.about: Lists the law and implementing ordinances in the compilation.
subfiles.summary: Index of the law and related imperial ordinances.

subfiles.title: Notes on the law and stockholding rules
subfiles.about: Summarizes the law’s coverage and its gasoline, heavy oil, and crude oil stockholding requirements.
subfiles.summary: Notes identify covered businesses, reserve quantities, storage periods, and tank requirements.

subfiles.title: Permits, approvals, and sanctions
subfiles.about: Lists activities requiring permission under the petroleum law.
subfiles.summary: Covers refining, importing, refinery capacity, storage exceptions, transfers, and business suspension.

subfiles.title: Outstanding reports
subfiles.about: Lists initial reports required from established oil importers and refiners.
subfiles.summary: Records 1934 deadlines for import plans, goods in transit, and business details.

subfiles.title: Current reports
subfiles.about: Lists recurring petroleum industry filing obligations.
subfiles.summary: Notes annual business plans and reports, stock plans, and monthly filings.

subfiles.title: Significant dates and duties
subfiles.about: Records key dates and duties associated with the oil law.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR chiefly preserves the law’s March 1934 enactment and enforcement references.

subfiles.title: Miscellaneous provisions
subfiles.about: Summarizes miscellaneous powers under the oil law.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary notes mention withheld permits and government powers.

subfiles.title: Offenses and penalties under the oil law
subfiles.about: Lists violations involving unauthorized business, reports, inspections, and official orders.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary checklist of punishable breaches of the law.

subfiles.title: The Petroleum Industry Law, No. 26 of 1934
subfiles.about: Sets out Japan’s petroleum refining and importing controls.
subfiles.summary: The law establishes permits, compulsory reserves, state powers over supply and prices, inspections, an industry committee, and penalties. Several pages of this copy are poorly legible.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 196 enforcing the Oil Industry Law
subfiles.about: Defines covered oil businesses, refinery capacity, import permissions, and reserve obligations.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance specifies eligible products and businesses, minimum refinery sizes, reserve quantities, and government purchase powers. It also addresses military and public interest orders.

subfiles.title: Overseas enforcement ordinance and abstract of the Oil Industry Law
subfiles.about: Extends the oil law to Korea, Formosa, and Sakhalin and summarizes selected provisions.
subfiles.summary: Records overseas enforcement from July 1, 1934, followed by an abstract of licensing and control powers.

subfiles.title: Organization of the Oil Industry Committee
subfiles.about: Defines the committee’s remit, membership, appointments, and staff.
subfiles.summary: The commerce minister chairs a committee of up to twenty members.

subfiles.title: Illegible compilation divider
subfiles.about: Separates sections of the petroleum law compilation.
subfiles.summary: Only an unclear heading survives in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Regulations for enforcement of the Oil Industry Law
subfiles.about: Specifies applications, business plans, reports, storage rules, and inspections for oil companies.
subfiles.summary: The regulations detail permits for refiners and importers, annual plans, monthly reports, product grades, reserve calculations, storage locations, exceptions, and business transfers or closures. The final page includes the form and legal basis for an inspector’s certificate.

subfiles.title: Japanese inspection certificate form
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Provides the Japanese form of an oil industry inspector’s certificate.
subfiles.summary: Certificate text and format for officials conducting inspections.

subfiles.title: Japanese text of the Oil Industry Law enforcement regulations
subfiles.about: Provides the Japanese original of the detailed oil industry enforcement rules.
subfiles.summary: These pages cover permissions, applications, business plans, reports, stockholding, storage, transfers, and transitional requirements. The scanned pages appear in reverse article order, and the OCR is especially fragmentary.

subfiles.title: Japanese ordinance on the Oil Industry Committee
subfiles.about: Provides Japanese provisions concerning the Oil Industry Committee.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary Japanese text addresses committee composition and administration.

subfiles.title: Japanese ordinance enforcing the Oil Industry Law
subfiles.about: Provides the Japanese original of implementing provisions on covered oil businesses and government powers.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines refining and importing, permits certain import exceptions, and addresses compulsory oil holdings and military consultation. The OCR is fragmentary.
